- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects downward; apply a 1–3% upward bias to subsequent days to avoid premature mean reversion.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; add 1–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model frequently overestimates 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 18-day average if sentiment is ≤0.5.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag in adjusting to sentiment shifts; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment flips from 0.67 to 0.00 or vice versa.
